title: Putin orders direct trade and political relations with Abkhazia and South Ossetia
body:
On 16 April 2008 Russian President Vladimir Putin issued a decree opening direct trade, transportation and political relations with the breakaway Georgian regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia. The measure was described as a response to Western recognition of Kosovo's declaration of independence in February 2008, and it came two weeks after the NATO summit in Bucharest.

A statement issued on 19 April 2008 by the Georgian Association in the USA, signed by Mamuka Tsereteli and Stephen Jones, called the decree a threat to Georgia, regional stability and international law. The statement listed earlier Russian actions that it said aimed at integrating the two territories, including military support for the separatist authorities, mass grants of Russian citizenship without consulting Georgia, an economic embargo and airspace violations. It argued that Georgia's offers of broad autonomy to both regions had been rejected by Moscow.

The statement also quoted foreign reactions. Senator John McCain was cited as saying Russia was pursuing de facto annexation. Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton was cited as calling Georgia a small democracy that must not be undermined and urging President Bush to send a senior envoy to Tbilisi. Members of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe were cited as saying the decision undermined Georgia's internationally recognised sovereignty. These characterisations are those of the Georgian diaspora organisation that issued the statement.
